## Requirements (from the spec)

1. `sqitch tag r11-sqitch-hygiene` + `sqitch rework
   shared_temporal_contract`: reworked deploy/revert are no-ops; reworked
   verify asserts the **27 named facets** this change installs (never a
   global count); `*@r11-sqitch-hygiene.sql` copies stay byte-identical
   to the landed scripts (cmp test); both new plan lines appended at EOF
   by sqitch, clock-stamped. (SIG-ENG-045)
2. Extension ownership (D-P32.16a-1): test + CI round trip deploy into a
   database created `TEMPLATE template0` — test extensions equal
   plan-owned extensions; no migration change. (SIG-ENG-045,
   SIG-STORE-041)
3. `make test-sqitch-roundtrip` + a CI python-job step: deploy → verify →
   `revert -y` → deploy → verify over the whole plan, all exit 0, every
   PR. (SIG-ENG-045)
4. Plan-date guard: a new plan line whose `planned_at` is later than its
   commit fails; L44–52 byte-identical to the P34.22a base fixture and
   pass only through the expiring `history.policy` allow entries; a
   verify-lint fails a verify script asserting a global count.
   (SIG-ENG-045, SIG-MEM-005)
5. Planner identity: new plan lines name the plan's existing planner
   identity (`Devin <devin@sig-project.org>`), set through
   `SQITCH_FULLNAME`/`SQITCH_EMAIL`, never the git user — a test fails a
   new line naming any other address.
6. `sqitch/sqitch` pinned by digest everywhere it appears
   (`sqitch/sqitch@sha256:f247ab0e…` — the `sqitch/sqitch:latest`
   resolution at writing, `docker pull` + `docker inspect` 2026-10-04).
7. Engineering ADR-196 (next free ≥ 191, ≠ ADR-195): the verify contract
   (assert what the change installs), extension ownership (the plan owns
   only the extensions it creates), one plan per cluster (roles are
   cluster-global; full revert drops them), C-10 (L44–52 never re-stamped;
   corrections by appended record). `## Revisit trigger` included.
8. Close D-P32.10a-1 and D-P32.16a-1 DONE through appended
   `obligation-event/1` transitions citing the CI round-trip log —
   applied at closeout, after the head's CI run exists.
9. Hosted head read: gated on the verbatim go — **not given** → per the
   contract's OM-19 clause there is **no queued leg**: the run records
   "hosted head not read here — P34.24b reads it from its clone".

## Hosted head read (not executed — the contract's fallback)

The ticket's named hosted read — `SELECT change, change_id, planned_at,
committed_at FROM sqitch.changes ORDER BY committed_at DESC LIMIT 5` —
was **not executed**: the operator's verbatim go was not given. Per the
contract's OM-19 clause this is **not** a queued leg: the fallback is
already specified — **P34.24b reads the hosted head from its PITR
clone** rehearsal. No production contact of any kind happened in this
run (no reads, no mutations — OM-14). AC6 is therefore honestly "not
claimed" rather than "deferred to a later leg".
